mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% in the month preceding the decision date reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the prior 20-day period when FEDFUNDS was below 4.0% (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which elevates consumer confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 2% month-over-month while UNRATE falls by at least 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant correlation with the labor strength signal (Pearson IC > 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) above 0.3% suggests accelerating demand growth, which elevates expected corporate profits and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite CPIAUCSL monthly growth exceeding 0.3% for the past 4 months (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of over 2% indicates weakening supply-side constraints, which reduces production costs and supports higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not higher than during the prior 20-day window when INDPRO was flat or rising (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate remains unchanged for three consecutive months during a tightening cycle, the market anticipates a near-term rate cut, causing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days to turn positive.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS unchanged for 3 months while yield curve steepens
regime_hint: early stage of rate hike cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain negative despite the rate hold and steepening curve (IC < -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.5% triggers a labor market tightening that raises wage growth expectations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4.5% in a single month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the prior 60 days when UNRATE was above 4.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales (implied by HOUST) exceeding 2% growth signal robust consumer demand, which elevates earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (IC < 0.15).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained interaction between a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and a rise in new home sales (implied by GDPC1) suggests easing supply constraints in manufacturing while housing demand is growing, which together produce positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
regime_hint: divergent supply and housing demand dynamics
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive when the interaction signal is present (IC < 0.1).
